title: Protecting Skin From Wet Concrete
summary: Wet concrete is caustic and can burn skin on contact, and chromium in cement can cause career-ending allergic reactions. This talk covers protective clothing, sealing gaps, and washing exposed skin.
talking_points: Wear protective clothing and gear: long-sleeve coveralls, waterproof boots tall enough to keep concrete out, alkali-resistant gloves, and safety glasses.
Pull sleeves down over gloves and tuck pants into boots. Tape the top of the boots to keep concrete out.
Use ready-mixed concrete instead of mixing on site when possible to cut contact during mixing.
Kneel on a dry board or waterproof kneepads on fresh concrete.
Remove rings and watches - wet concrete collects under them and burns the skin.
If concrete gets on your skin, wash it right away with pH-neutral soap and clean water. Do not use the water in the bucket or hand sanitizer. Wash work clothes separately at home.
site_hazards_to_check: Workers without waterproof boots, alkali-resistant gloves, or eye protection
Gaps at sleeve cuffs and boot tops where concrete can get in
No clean water and pH-neutral soap on site for washing exposed skin
Rings, watches, or wristbands worn during concrete work
Kneeling directly on fresh concrete with no board or waterproof kneepads
discussion_questions: What PPE keeps wet concrete off your skin, and is everyone wearing it?
Where is the clean water and pH-neutral soap if concrete gets on your skin?
Why should you not rinse concrete off using the water in the mixing bucket?
